conclusions.rationale: The two exact assertion invocations provide useful Step 1 primitive evidence: occupied passive inspection leaves fixture store bytes unchanged, and a current-session negative remains Uncertain. They do not invoke handy settings, observe unavailable/5 on an older owner, or exercise authenticated live routing, the five-second unknown-outcome timeout, live effects, UI notification, offline application under the shared lock/validation, or live-only unavailability. The source explicitly labels these bindings partial. Selecting the whole AC-005 identity does not narrow its normative criterion to two subclauses. Consequently full AC-005 execution acceptance remains missing even if both primitive tests pass. This is not a source-quality defect in the approved Step 1 scope, and unavailable foreign native observations are not used as blockers.

source_citations.excerpt: When a Handy instance of the same user and settings store is running, the CLI sends the operation to it over a local channel accessible only to that user and waits up to 5 seconds for its answer; the instance applies it with its live state, re-registers affected shortcuts and notifies its UI.

findings.description: The generated mapping binds partial passive-probe assertions to the entire AC-005, while the required live-channel/offline CLI behavior is absent from this test source. A covered verdict would overstate feature acceptance.
findings.suggestion: Preserve Step 1 as direct primitive execution evidence and Partial in implementation tracking; supply a fresh independent whole-AC mapping once the routing, repository and native integration steps are implemented. Do not invent whole-AC coverage or alter the approved criterion to unblock an interim step.
